- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If recent true outcomes show sharp downward spikes after high peaks, model should adjust downward with lagged momentum correction.  
- When official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model should not ignore policy count (even if 0) — adjust for policy-induced volatility.  
- If model forecast is flat or slowly rising while true outcome shows strong mean reversion, increase downward bias in early horizon.  
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model should not assume linear continuation — apply exponential decay to recent highs.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should avoid overfitting to recent sentiment — use rolling average of sentiment to smooth forecast.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome in early days of a 30d window, adjust for lagged sentiment impact — add 0.1–0.2 to forecast for first 5 days.  
- For high event count with low bullish sentiment, model should not overcorrect — allow for 5–10% downward buffer in early forecast.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, model should not follow the spike — apply “safety margin” to forecast by 5–10% below peak.  
- When policy_count > 0, model should reduce forecast volatility — apply 0.5–1.0% smoothing to forecast path.
